problem: Object detectors used as perception front-ends for RL goal navigation (e.g. YOLO variants) are too large and energy-hungry for edge devices, and no prior work combines Mamba, knowledge distillation and architecture optimization to get a detector small enough to fit in cache.
motivation: Autonomous robots need real-time, low-power perception on devices like Jetson Orin Nano and Raspberry Pi 5. Passing detector bounding boxes to an RL policy is a compact state representation, but the detector's overhead dominates edge cost. Mamba/SSMs offer attention-free long-range modeling with lower compute.
key_idea: Build a lightweight Mamba (Lite-Conv-SSM with LiteSS2D) object detector, distill it into a much smaller student, and feed its bounding boxes to a PPO policy for goal-directed navigation.
insight: Distilling the teacher (2.4M params, 9.1 MB, 0.47 GFLOPs) into a student (639k params, 2.5 MB, 0.15 GFLOPs) keeps mAP at 0.93, and cuts energy per inference by 63% (Jetson) and 73% (Pi 5). Detector size, not the policy, is what drives edge cost, and compact BBOX states suffice for simple navigation. There is no ablation of the KD loss terms or the LiteSS2D design, so the evidence is limited to teacher-vs-student comparison.
method: Sim-to-real goal navigation framework: detector outputs normalized BBOXes for n objects (1x4n), concatenated with a one-hot goal (n) and last action (a) into a (5n+a) state vector for a PPO policy with actions {left, right, forward}.
Reward shaping: +10 goal reached, -2 wrong goal/wall collision, -0.01 per step, distance-change reward, first-goal-visibility +0.1, small exploration bonuses.
Lite-Conv-SSM block: convolution branch (depthwise + pointwise) for local features and an SSM branch (LiteSS2D) for global features; outputs concatenated and channel-shuffled.
LiteSS2D: four-direction selective scan (expand, shared S6 core, merge) with weights shared across directions, factorized convs and reused Mamba matrices, adapted from VMamba/MedMambaLite.
Hierarchical backbone: patch embedding, stages of Lite-Conv-SSM blocks, patch merging, and a light conv+pooling+linear detection head.

Knowledge distillation: frozen teacher, student loss L = L_det + 1.0*L_KD (temperature-2 KL on class logits) + 0.25*L_feat (MSE on intermediate features); the student uses depths [2,2,4,2] and channels (32,64,128,256).
Edge deployment: student exported to ONNX and profiled for energy/latency on Jetson Orin Nano and Raspberry Pi 5.

setting.backbone: EdgeNavMamba-ST (Mamba detector, distilled from EdgeNavMamba-TR) + PPO policy, both trained from scratch
setting.training_data: Custom shapes dataset: 1,800 real-world images and ~5,500 MiniWorld images (red/blue/black boxes, 90/10 split); PPO trained 500k timesteps in MiniWorld
setting.observation: monocular RGB image resized to 224x224, reduced to bounding boxes

numbers_note: Navigation success rates are from a figure/text, computed over the last 100 training episodes, not a held-out benchmark. Energy results (63% Jetson, 73% Pi 5) appear only in a figure and text. There are no standard benchmark results.
results: The distilled student matches the teacher's mAP of 0.93 with about 73% fewer parameters (639k vs 2.4M), 2.5 MB size, and 63%/73% lower energy per inference on Jetson Orin Nano/Pi 5. It has 31% fewer parameters than the Squeezed Edge YOLO baseline (931k, mAP 0.95). PPO navigation in MiniWorld reaches 100/94/90% success with 1/2/3 objects.
limitations: Toy evaluation: colored boxes in a simple room, a custom small dataset, and no standard navigation benchmarks or held-out episodes.
No ablations of KD losses or LiteSS2D, and lower mAP (0.93) than YOLOv5s (0.96) and Squeezed Edge YOLO (0.95); the real-robot navigation claim is not demonstrated (only edge profiling).
Inconsistent numbers: '67% size reduction' vs. the table (9.1 to 2.5 MB is about 73%), and state vector scales with the number of objects.
